issues.failure_explanation: Lemma 2.1 asserts strict increase of phi with no relation between h and delta^mu. On I^j the affine coefficient is (h-delta^mu); if delta^mu>h (permitted by the stated setup, e.g. mu=1/4, delta=1/25, N=5 gives delta^mu≈0.447>0.2=h), then phi(t_j^delta)=jh+delta^mu>(j+1)h=phi(t_{j+1}) and phi decreases on I^j, so the claim fails. In the boundary case delta^mu=h (allowed by Theorem 2.2's hypothesis h>=delta^mu, and used in every numerical test: "mu so that h=delta^mu"), the second piece of (2.7) is constant, so phi - and hence every psi_q - is constant on each sub-interval I^j: Theorem 2.2's "strictly increasing" and "psi_q'(x) only vanishes at the endpoints of G_q^j and I_q^j" fail, and the advertised strict monotonicity (feature (i)) is contradicted by the paper's own numerical regime.

issues.overall_effect: The (strict) monotonicity claims of Lemma 2.1 and Theorem 2.2 hold only after adding h>=delta^mu (monotonicity) and h>delta^mu (strictness); the strict-increase selling point excludes the degenerate flat case delta^mu=h that all numerics use. (ii) The premise "y_{j_p} all rational numbers" is false in general: the values involve the free real parameters h=N*delta, delta^mu and phi((1-q)delta). (iii) The assertion is false across levels in the paper's own computational regime: when delta^mu=h (used in all numerics, e.g. mu=1/2, delta=1/N^2), (2.14) gives phi((1-q)delta)=0 for every q, so psi_q(c_q^{j_p})=j_p h+(h+delta^mu)/2 is independent of q and a_q^{\bs j}=a_{q'}^{\bs j} for all q != q' - the opposite of distinct. Remark dist-again's claim that the explicit formulas readily verify the proposition fails for the same reason.

issues.failure_explanation: The per-level bound |(s_{k+1}-s_k)S(z)|<=|s_{k+1}-s_k| in (2.37) (and (2.39)) needs z=(Psi_q(x)-tau_k)/(tau_{k+1}-tau_k) in [0,1] (where |S|<=1) with tau_k=a_q^{\bs j} the containing cube's image; this localization is never proved and is false under the construction's own rules. Since psi_q strictly increases by h-delta^mu across each I_q^{j_p} (from phi(t_j^delta)=t_j+delta^mu to phi(t_{j+1})=t_{j+1}), Psi_q varies over a cube by up to |lambda|_1(h-delta^mu), so |Psi_q(x)-a_q^{\bs j}| reaches ≈|lambda|_1 h/2, while (2.30) selects the segment of length ≈lambda_min h - with the paper's Sprecher-like choice lambda_1=1/(J+2), lambda_1 h≈h/J: hence z is outside [0,1] for typical x (e.g. x_2 at an endpoint of I_q^{j_2} gives |z|≈J/2), S is evaluated outside its defining interval where |S(z)|~|z|, and the estimate collapses (the literal per-level bound sums to O(h^{alpha-1}), divergent for alpha<1). Independently, the argmin in (2.29) minimizes image distance, which along the fine (lambda_1) direction is attained by centers up to Theta(1) away in physical space (e.g. with x_2 at the left edge of I_q^{j_2}, the nearest image is attained at a center with c^{i_1}≈x_1+lambda_2 h/(2 lambda_1)≈x_1+1/2), so even the first term |f(x)-f(c_q^{\bs i})|/N is Theta(1/N) per level, giving an O(1) total error: as specified, the scheme need not converge. The same root falsifies Remark remk-Slides: the deviation up to lambda_2 h/2 beyond row-band edges lands Psi_q(x) strictly inside the inter-row gaps it claims are never entered, so the whole-data C^2 interpolation endorsed there bridges data from centers more than distance 1 apart (the paper's own "dislocation"). The advertised C^2-continuity of g_q o Psi_q(x) is also unestablished, since the argmin selection rule switches segments along hypersurfaces where the evaluated function is discontinuous. (The numerical tests sidestep the defect by taking delta^mu=h, which makes the inner functions constant on the I_q^j - cf. ISSUE-001 - so Psi_q is constant on each cube and z=0.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the min-distance rule in (2.30) by the coarse direction p*=argmax_p lambda_p through the containing (or physically closest) cube and use the segment of that row bracketing Psi_q(x); prove a contained localization lemma: |Psi_q(x)-a_q^{\bs j}|<=|lambda|_1(h-delta^mu)/2 (plus delta^mu-terms in gaps) and node spacings are >=lambda_{p*} tilde h, so the bracketing nodes correspond to centers within O(dh) of x (index offset <=|lambda|_1/(2 lambda_{p*})<=d/2); then |f(x)/N-g_q o Psi_q(x)|<=(C_alpha/N)(C_d h)^alpha and summing restores ||f-f_N||_infty=O(h^alpha) with a d-dependent constant.
issues.overall_effect: The main error estimate (3.3) - hence the abstract's O(N^{-alpha(1+gamma)}) guarantee, intro feature (iii), the refinement (3.4), and the claim of an affirmative answer to Demb-Sprecher - is unproven for the construction as specified (Definition 2.7, rules (2.29)-(2.30), Algorithm 1 step III(ii)); the gap-level estimate (2.35)/(2.39), which uses the image-closest cube, inherits the same failure; Remark 2.8's justification of whole-data C^2 interpolation for Sprecher-like lambda is false; the advertised C^2 smoothness of the superpositions is undelivered.
issues.title: Main error estimate requires Psi_q(x) to lie in the chosen interpolation segment, which fails under the construction's selection rules
issues.why_classification: The repair changes the algorithm's selection rule and requires a new but contained localization lemma; the theorem's statement - rate O(h^alpha), hypotheses on lambda, and scope - survives verbatim, with only a worse d-dependent constant, so there is no loss of regime or rate but more than a local patch is needed.

(ii) In (2.35), a point in a gap adjacent to I_q^{j_p} is up to (h+delta)/2=(N+1)delta/2 per coordinate from the nearest center, so the bound should be sqrt(d)(N+1)delta/2, not sqrt(d) N delta/2.
